analysis: Schizophrenia is primarily treated with anti-psychotic medications, which are well-established as the first-line treatment for managing the core symptoms of the disorder, such as hallucinations and delusions. While anti-depressants may be used for co-occurring depressive symptoms, they are not effective for treating the primary symptoms of schizophrenia. Anti-epileptics and mood stabilizers are not standard treatments for schizophrenia and have limited roles in its management. Therefore, based on the consensus in the medical community, the most appropriate treatment option for schizophrenia is anti-psychotics.
